Subject: Draft RCA & corrective actions — Celestis incident (attached)

Jordan / team,

Attached is the initial RCA (celestis_rca_v1.pdf) and the action tracker (mapp_celestis_v1.xlsx). TL;DR: a combination of an unexpected request pattern (bursting large export batches with long seq length) and a suboptimal kernel route on one of the dedicated inferencers caused KV cache churn and de-optimized batching. This produced lower throughput and higher tail latencies under realistic load.

Root cause summary:
- Primary: model kernel selector chose a fallback slow path for ~18% of tokens due to sequence-length skew after a client-side change in payload ordering.
- Secondary: cache eviction thresholds were below recommended levels for Celestis's traffic shape.
- Contributing: a delayed autoscaling decision due to a spike in short-lived connections.

Immediate actions (owner / ETA):
- [Vivek] Adjust kernel routing rules and redeploy optimized kernels — 4 hrs (INF-7781).
- [Hannah] Increase KV cache thresholds and enable sticky routing for Celestis — 3 hrs.
- [Mateo] Failover Celestis to reserved pool and apply throttles for large export batches — 30 min (done).
- [Laura] Deliver exec readout and update SLA remediation credits proposal — EOD.

Attachments: celestis_rca_v1.pdf, server_perf_trace_20260301.zip, mapp_celestis_v1.xlsx

We will post detailed traces to JIRA INF-7781 and update the HubSpot ticket HS: 0045921.

- Laura Bennett
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
